paper.title: Sparse Linear Bandits with Blocking Constraints

settings.name_in_paper: High-dimensional sparse linear bandits with blocking constraint (soft sparsity)
unmapped: Blocking constraint: each arm can be pulled at most once
Regret is measured against the sum of the T arms with the highest distinct means (top-T unique arms)
Soft sparsity: theta need not be exactly sparse; its relative l1 tail beta_k at sparsity level k is unknown to the learner
The learner (BSLB) knows the sparsity level k, a lower bound lambda^l on the optimal minimum eigenvalue lambda*, and R_max for tuning the exploration period
settings.definition_quote:
At each round $\timeindex\in [\numrounds]$, an arm $\arm_\timeindex$  which has not been pulled in the first $\timeindex-1$ rounds is selected by the online algorithm (decision-maker). Note that such a selection mechanism respects the blocking constraint. 
Subsequently, the arm $a_t$ is pulled and the algorithm observes the stochastic reward $\reward_\timeindex$. 
We model the expected reward $\bb{E}r_t$  as a linear function of the arm embedding where $\parameter\in \R^\dimarm$ is an unknown parameter vector. In particular, the random variable $\reward_\timeindex$ is generated according to
 $\reward_\timeindex = \langle\parameter, \arm_\timeindex \rangle + \noise_\timeindex$ where $\{\noise_\timeindex\}_{t\in [T]}$ are zero-mean sub-gaussian random variables independent across rounds with variance proxy bounded from above by $\sigma^2$.

settings.name_in_paper: High-dimensional sparse linear bandits with blocking constraint, exactly k-sparse (lower bound)
unmapped: Blocking constraint: each arm can be pulled at most once (arm multiset allowed)
Regret is measured against the top-T unique arms
settings.definition_quote: Consider the d-dimensional sparse linear bandits framework with blocking constraint having a set A subseteq B^d of M arms spanning R^d and T rounds (T << d << M). ... eta_t is zero-mean independent noise random variable with variance sigma^2 = 1. Assume that the parameter vector is k-sparse.

algorithms.name: BSLB (Blocked Sparse Linear Bandits, Explore-Then-Commit with Lasso)
C-BSLB (CORRAL over BSLB instances on exponential sparsity grid)

symbols.lambda_star: max over arm subsets of the minimum eigenvalue of the normalized Gram matrix (eq. discreteopt)
symbols.beta_k: relative l1 tail of theta at sparsity level k: ||theta_{T_k^c}||_1/||theta_{T_k}||_1
symbols.k_sparse: sparsity level k chosen as input (not necessarily exact sparsity)

source.label: th:regret

results.notes: Regret is with respect to the top-T unique arms; expectation is over the algorithm's randomness and the regret is defined through means, so recorded as pseudo-regret. The comparator best_feasible_policy is used because the regret benchmark is the best T distinct arms. Compute: GetGoodSubset is poly in M but exponential in d (brute-force subset search); without that search the bound worsens by a factor (lambda_l)^{-2} (Remark 4).

symbols.lambda_star: max over arm subsets of the minimum eigenvalue of the normalized Gram matrix

source.label: coro:hard

results.notes: The exponent of lambda_star (-1) differs from Theorem 3 (-2/3), so this is recorded separately. The paper writes O rather than O_tilde here.

symbols.lambda_A: minimum-eigenvalue quantity lambda_min(A) of the arm set (as in Hao et al. 2020)

conditions: arms in unit ball spanning R^d

source.label: thm:lower
source.quote: Assume that the parameter vector is $k$-sparse, $\Vert \theta \Vert_0 = k$. Then for any bandit algorithm the worst case regret is lower bounded as follows, $\mathbb{E}[\mathsf{R}] = \Omega(\min((\mineigvalue(\mathcal{A}))^{-1/3}k^{1/3}\mathsf{T}^{2/3}),\sqrt{d\mathsf{T}}))$.

results.notes: Proved by reduction from Hao et al. (2020) Theorem 3.3: each arm is copied T times in a multiset. The printed parentheses are malformed; the intended min of the two terms is recorded. In the data-poor regime the bound reduces to the first term.

symbols.k_star: optimal sparsity parameter minimizing the Theorem 3 bound
symbols.Reg_star: expected regret (bound) of BSLB run with optimal sparsity k_star
symbols.R_best: regret bound of the best base algorithm, used to set the CORRAL learning rate

tuning: base BSLB instances with k in {2^i}_{i=0}^{floor(log2 d)+1}
appropriate CORRAL learning rate eta = min(1/(40 T R_best), sqrt(floor(log2 d)/T))

source.label: th:corralling
source.quote: Let the \texttt{C-BSLB} algorithm ... run with an appropriate learning rate on multiple versions of \texttt{BSLB}, using distinct sparsity parameter $\sparsityk$ taking values in the set $\{2^i\}_{i=0}^{\lfloor \log_2(\dimarm)\rfloor+1}$. ... Then the meta-algorithm \texttt{C-BSLB} achieves the following regret guarantee, $\expectedregret = \orderof(\sqrt{\numrounds\log_2(\dimarm)}+\sqrt{\sparsity}\log_2(\dimarm)\bestregret)$.

results.notes: The bound is relative to the regret of the oracle-best BSLB, so it does not need knowledge of k. log2 is written as log/log(2).
